source.title: Structural Inference: Interpreting Small Language Models with Susceptibilities
source.authors: Garrett Baker; George Wang; Jesse Hoogland; Daniel Murfet

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses previously identified induction-circuit heads as a reference for evaluating its susceptibility-based structural-inference method. Its own results measure susceptibility patterns, not induction copying or the mechanism itself.
record.gate_note: The paper reports associations between induction-pattern tokens and head susceptibilities, and says its PCA recovers a structure associated with the previously identified induction circuit. These are susceptibility results, not direct measurements of attention to an earlier copy, copying the following token, induction-head formation, in-context-learning gains, or a loss bump. The circuit identifications attributed to Wang et al. are cited findings, not results to record here.
record.test_reason: The paper develops susceptibility-based structural inference and uses the induction circuit identified in prior work (Wang et al. 2024) as a known reference module to validate the method. Its results are susceptibility PCA loadings and distributions, not measurements of induction behaviour (attention to earlier copy, copying), formation timing, in-context-learning gains, or loss bumps. Head identities per seed come from cited prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that susceptibilities, estimated with local SGLD, give per-token attribution scores, and that PCA of the response matrix separates known functional modules such as multigram and induction heads in a 3M-parameter transformer. They interpret PC2 as the induction circuit expressing induction patterns that other heads, including the layer-1 multigram heads, suppress, and report that this holds across four seeds. They present this as validation of the method, not as a test of induction-head formation or of its role in in-context learning.
record.recipe_differences: Uses local SGLD susceptibility estimates and PCA of head responses to data-distribution and token-pattern changes, rather than directly measuring induction-head formation, attention/copying, or the loss and in-context-learning trajectories in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The analysis separates layers and varies probe datasets and training checkpoints. The paper also reports that per-token susceptibility changes with context length, especially for layer-1 multigram heads.

fits_no_version.finding: In a 3M two-layer attention-only transformer, per-token susceptibility PCA PC2 loads positively on heads previously identified as the induction circuit (1:6, 1:7, 0:1, 0:4, 0:5) and negatively on other heads, across four seeds; layer-1 multigram heads show positive (suppression) susceptibility on induction-pattern tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Susceptibility-based structural inference recovers a previously identified induction circuit and associates it with expression of induction patterns, while other layer-1 heads suppress them.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-token susceptibilities on an induction example show the pattern while zero-ablation loss differences and raw loss do not; overall correlation of susceptibility with ablation delta is negligible.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Per-token susceptibilities carry induction-pattern signal not visible in zero-ablation or loss attribution in this model.

record.problems: The study analyzes a small 3M-parameter model. It reports susceptibility estimates from approximate, correlated SGLD samples and states that the effects of SGLD hyperparameter selection remain poorly understood. The induction-circuit interpretation relies on circuit identifications from prior work; the study does not directly measure induction copying or in-context-learning performance.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were included because they concern other token patterns, datasets, or components without an explicit result about induction-pattern susceptibility or the induction-circuit-associated structure.

untested.parts: Whether heads attend to and copy the token after an earlier occurrence, or form via composition with previous-token heads (composition taken from Wang et al.).
Abrupt formation, coincidence with ICL gain, loss bump; susceptibility trajectories over checkpoints are not analysed for formation timing.
Role of induction heads in most in-context learning in large models.
Recurrence of induction behaviour across families/sizes; the four seeds' induction heads are identified in cited prior work, not here.
Dependence of formation on data or training setup.
Whether few-shot task learning runs through other mechanisms.
Whether formation is a sequence of sub-steps.

record.verdict_notes: The study builds on Wang et al. 2024 and Hoogland et al. 2025, which may test V2/V7 on the same models; this paper itself does not. Context-length growth of susceptibility for multigram heads (Fig. 10) is suggestive but is not an ICL measure. Code release is not stated; the datasets are on HuggingFace.

versions.untested_parts: Whether heads attend to the token after an earlier copy, copy it, or form by composing with previous-token heads.
Abrupt formation, its timing relative to in-context-learning gains, and the training-loss bump.
Whether induction heads carry most in-context learning in large transformers.

Whether induction behaviour itself recurs across model families, sizes, architectures, or modalities; the paper reports susceptibility-PCA associations across seeds, not direct induction-behaviour tests.
Whether induction formation or persistent in-context learning depends on training data or setup.
Whether few-shot task learning is carried mainly by other heads or mechanisms.
Whether induction-head formation consists of multiple steps or overlapping transitions.

rows.subject: 3M-parameter two-layer attention-only transformer, seed 1
rows.stage_stated: trained on next-token prediction; per-token susceptibility PCA at checkpoint step 49900
rows.operation_detail: PCA of per-token susceptibilities, separately by layer
rows.measure: PC2 association between data-pattern loadings and attention-head susceptibility loadings
rows.value: Text reports induction patterns on the data side and positive PC2 loadings on the heads identified by Wang et al. as the induction circuit; remaining heads have negative loadings. Word endings have the opposite pattern association.
rows.locator: Section 4.2, PC2: The induction circuit; Figure 3
rows.note: This is an association in the susceptibility PCA, not a direct test that heads perform induction copying.
rows.check: Susceptibility-PCA association with heads labelled as induction by Wang et al.; measures method's recovery of a known module, not induction behaviour. Also note text: in data, PC2 has word endings positive and induction patterns negative (record's phrasing of data-side sign is loose). State relative to any version cannot be determined.

rows.subject: 3M-parameter two-layer attention-only transformer, seed 2

rows.note: The paper states that the induction-circuit appearance in this analysis holds across all four seeds. The figure plots PCA loadings; the cited seed-specific head identities are attributed to Wang et al.
rows.check: Figure-only PCA loadings for seed 2; validation of method against cited head identities (Wang et al. Appendix G), not a test of induction behaviour.

rows.subject: 3M-parameter two-layer attention-only transformer, seed 1
rows.stage_stated: training checkpoints listed in Section C.3
rows.operation_detail: Joint trajectory PCA of head susceptibilities across datasets and training checkpoints
rows.measure: PC2 head loadings in susceptibility-trajectory PCA
rows.value: Text reports PC2 separates the layer-1 multigram heads from the induction heads; three PCs explain 98% of variance, with PC2 explaining 10.76%.
rows.note: The trajectory is of susceptibilities, not a measurement of induction formation or in-context learning.
rows.check: Trajectory PCA over training of susceptibilities; checks the method's separation of head groups, does not measure induction-head formation timing or ICL. Record's PC3 loading on induction heads (1:6, 1:7) is not mentioned; PC2 loads on 0:1 and multigram heads.

rows.subject: 3M-parameter two-layer attention-only transformer, seed 1
rows.operation_detail: Compared per-token susceptibility distributions for induction-pattern tokens with distributions for all tokens
rows.value: Text reports that the distribution shifts right for layer-1 multigram heads and, to a lesser extent, head 1:6; Figure 16–17 plot per-head distributions and means.
rows.note: The reported shift concerns susceptibility values on induction-pattern tokens, not the heads' direct copying behaviour.
rows.check: Susceptibility distribution shift on induction-pattern tokens (e.g. l1h0 mean 0.78 to 6.28; l1h6 0.20 to 3.00; l1h7 0.11 to 1.83); not a measure of induction behaviour.

rows.subject: 3M-parameter two-layer attention-only transformer, seed 1, head 1:4
rows.operation_detail: Compared per-token susceptibility, zero-ablation loss difference, and original token loss on an example containing an induction pattern
rows.measure: Whether the induction pattern is discernible in susceptibility, ablation-loss difference, and original token loss
rows.value: Text reports the induction pattern is particularly visible in positive susceptibilities, with no discernible pattern in zero-ablation loss differences or original per-token loss.
rows.note: This compares pattern-linked susceptibility with loss measures; it does not establish direct induction computation.
rows.check: Qualitative single-example comparison of susceptibility vs ablation loss for head 1:4; method comparison, not a test of the claim.
